facts.statement: Paleontologist Dong Zhiming described the small theropod Tugulusaurus faciles in 1973.
facts.quote: In 1973 a number of these were described by paleontologist Dong Zhiming, among them the bones of a small theropod which he named Tugulusaurus faciles.

facts.statement: The generic name Tugulusaurus refers to the Tugulu Group.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Tugulu Group.

facts.statement: The specific name faciles means "easily moving" and refers to the animal's agility indicated by its delicate bones.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Latin facilis, here with the meaning of "easily moving", referring to the agility of the animal as indicated by its "delicate bones".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V4025 was found in the Lianmuqin Formation dating from the Barremian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V4025, was found in layers of the Lianmuqin Formation dating from the Barremian–Albian.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype measures about 215 mm in length.
facts.quote: The femur has a length of about 215 mm.

facts.statement: The left first metacarpal is very short, measuring 26 mm.
facts.quote: The left first metacarpal is very short: 26 mm.

facts.statement: Tugulusaurus was an early alvarezsaur likely measuring between 1.9 and 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Tugulusaurus was an early alvarezsaur, likely measuring at 1.9-3 m in length.

facts.statement: Tugulusaurus was likely an agile animal with long legs that aided in reaching high speeds to chase prey or escape threats.
facts.quote: It was an agile animal, likely having long legs, which would aid in reaching high speeds, in order to chase prey and retreat from potential threats.

facts.statement: As an alvarezsauroid, Tugulusaurus likely used its long claws to dig into wood or dirt to find food.
facts.quote: Being an alvarezsauroid, it likely used its long claws to dig and tear into wood or dirt in order to find food.

facts.statement: Dong originally classified Tugulusaurus as a member of the Ornithomimidae within the Coelurosauria in 1973.
facts.quote: Tugulusaurus was originally classified by Dong in 1973 as a member of the Ornithomimidae, within the Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: In 2005, Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing concluded that Tugulusaurus is a valid genus of basal coelurosaurian with unknown affinities.
facts.quote: However, in 2005 Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing concluded that it is a valid genus of basal coelurosaurian of unknown affinities.

facts.statement: A 2018 cladistic analysis by Xu et al. recovered Tugulusaurus as a member of Alvarezsauria.
facts.quote: In their cladistic analysis of the newly described taxa Bannykus and Xiyunykus, Xu et al. (2018) recovered Tugulusaurus as a member of Alvarezsauria.

facts.statement: Tugulusaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 122 and 100 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 122 a 100 desde finales del Aptiense al Albiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Tugulusaurus is from the Valanginian to the Albian, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton represents the only known remains of the species Tugulusaurus faciles.
facts.quote: The skeleton represents the only remains of the species that have ever been discovered.
